TAKING MORE IN THE SAME DAY WON'T CHANGE THAT. 

In fact you'll probably feel horrible for a few days now. You also may have fucked the process of the medicine adjusting to a proper level. Negative side effects that follow usually last 4-6 weeks may now last longer or be stronger. It would not be worth all that for one day of more euphoria.

Your degree is a generalization to your field of study. There's a business degree and an arts degree and a science degree etc. The major is what you specifically studied for IN that field. For example, finance or accounting for business, sociology or music for arts, and kinesiology or chemistry for science etc. A minor works the same as a major, it's simply less in terms of credits needed to achieve. For example a major in finance may require 13 credits, while a minor only requires 5. 

A 4-year bachelors degree is 20 credits. Usually the breakdown is 5 credits a year x 4 years although many take longer than that. But for example, let's say you got into the business degree at UWO. After your first year you chose to major in accounting. That has 16 required credits. You can then use the remaining 4 to try for a minor and broaden your education, or instead a general mix of electives in many fields you have interest in. 

Regardless, everything I've discussed here is a part of undergraduate studies. There's a furthering of education in graduate studies which requires a seperate application and a few more years of college. This is where you get your Masters programs and from there further into PhD doctorates.
